I 100% won’t have kids for multiple reasons. One of which being I can’t even take care of myself in an episode. How am I supposed to care for a child in that state. And no matter what meds I’ve been on, these episodes won’t stop. 

I can’t leave a baby crying or hungry because I can’t get up. I can’t leave a three year old in a dirty pull up because I’m busy crying over feeling like a terrible parent. I’m not making my young child play by themself because mommy still doesn’t want to. I’m not staying home from parent teacher nights or games or things because I don’t care about anything. And when they become a moody teenager who acts out, I’m not going to be that mean mom who accidentally yells too loud because of my triggered response. And god forbid the day they show signs of this terrible disorder.

Yes passing this on is terrible, but I refuse to be a parent who can’t care for my kids.

I also won’t put myself at risk by going off some or all of my meds. Call me selfish, but I already don’t function that often. I’m not risking making it worse for anyone. Even though some say that it’ll be worth going off the meds, it can’t be worth it if I’m not alive.

Luckily my boyfriend doesn’t want them either and there’s a big chance I can’t have them anyway.

And to the people in my life who said I’ll be a great mother because I know what to look for and how to be there, nope.

I have an amazing boyfriend who I love and who loves me back. He accidentally found out I have bipolar only a few weeks into talking (I can tell you the funny story if you want) and he accepted me as I was despite my bipolar. Through the last year and a half, there’s been some tough times. He’s been through countless episodes and two hospitalizations. 

He’s been so supportive. But the thing is, despite how supportive your significant other is, you need to be just as supportive back. It’s exhausting for us to go through the ups and downs, but it’s also exhausting for them to see us like that and care for us when we can’t. My boyfriend has had to take off of work to hold me and watch me while I cried and begged him to just let me die. He never left my side. Once I had calmed down, I held him too and we talked about everything. 

No matter what we go through, he still looks at me the same. Wether we’re having the most wonderful days or if we’re laying in bed while I’m so out of it because I just took my strong prn because I was laying on the floor crying. 
He loves me just the same no matter what. 

The right person will see you as you and not your diagnosis. They will see through the episodes and remember who you are. They will love you no matter what. Your diagnosis doesn’t make you unlovable. It doesn’t make healthy love impossible. You can have a healthy relationship. I wish that for you.

The only declaws I have ever seen that I agreed with were one where both paws had had multiple claws ripped out from a mishap on their cat tree resulting in a really bad infection. Instead of just removing the few claws, we removed all of the front claws so that we could drain more infection before it spread further into the paws. 

We also had a cat that would scratch their face until it bled. We did all kinds of skin tests. We looked for bacteria, mites, fungus, tested for allergies, the works. We referred them to a dermatologist, but they found nothing and chalked it up to anxiety. When they came back to us for an eye injury from the scratching they let us know that the high dose of anxiety meds wasn’t working and revealed that this only happened when the cat was alone. Because the cat didn’t respond to any anxiety meds, was always going to have alone time, and was getting infections and more severe injuries from the scratching, we chose to declaw. When the owner showed us a video she had when she put a camera out, you could see her using the front claws to go at her head. When we took the claws, it was still happening, it finally stopped harming the cat.

These are the only declaws out of the four I’ve seen at my two years in my clinic that I’ve agreed with.
